newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse to raise margin calls, forced sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse to raise margin calls, forced sales.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand said on Monday it will raise margin calls to 35 percent from the current 25 percent effective on August 1.
The SET said in a statement it will also increase the percentage for forced sales to 25 percent from 15 percent on the same date.

The hike in margin call and forced sale percentages came after the SET last week had widened its daily floor/ceiling trading limit to 30 percent from an existing 10 percent effective from August 1, the statement said.
Margin trading enables investors to trade shares without having to pay up for all of the value of shares dealt.
A margin call is a demand made by brokerages of investors whose margain account has fallen below the minimum requirement.

Under the forced sale rule, brokers are permitted to force indebted clients to sell off shares when the share prices fell below a specified level in order to raise funds to repay debts borrowed from brokerages for share trading.
